decision: Bind the real Qubes resource-calibration CLI to the benchmark-derived synthetic DAG workload and require both workload-control and resource-probe qrexec services.

reviews.preferred: Require missions, durations, topology, resource service and workload service; derive the exact per-worker schedule with buildOrchestrationCalibrationPlan; start the workload before sampling and stop/reconcile it afterward.
reviews.why: Idle-only samples can materially understate RAM/CPU and produce a false resource-readiness result even when the collector itself requires workload evidence.

reviews.preferred: Reuse dig.SyntheticWorkload and its bounded stop/status reconciliation instead of introducing shell workload commands or a new daemon.
reviews.why: This preserves the existing bounded command schema, avoids arbitrary code execution, and retains positive cleanup confirmation after ambiguous stop responses.

reviews.preferred: Reuse the existing benchmark plan, workload hooks and read-only ResourceProbe in one CLI path.
reviews.why: No extra Qubes service is added, healthy-path qrexec traffic is only the workload start/stop already required for truthful calibration, and MissionQueue/coordinator semantics are unchanged.

alternativesRejected.approach: Keep the CLI resource-probe-only and rely on operators to start a workload manually.
alternativesRejected.reason: Not reproducible or fail-closed; an operator mistake silently measures idle Qubes.

alternativesRejected.approach: Generate a generic CPU burn independent of the orchestration benchmark.
alternativesRejected.reason: Lower fidelity: it does not reproduce the worker assignment, contention or mission timing used by the topology evaluator.
Higher operational and attack surface, persistent resource cost, and unnecessary regression risk at the current lab stage.

required: CLI config rejects missing workload service, missions or durations instead of falling back to idle sampling
runtime derives the expected 210ms-equivalent two-worker plan from the same DAG benchmark fixture
both worker Qubes receive workload start and stop commands through dig.SyntheticWorkload
resource samples use dig.ResourceProbe while the workload lifecycle is active
existing lost-stop-response reconciliation and cleanup tests remain green
qa.expectedImpact: No MissionQueue/coordinator behavior change; added CLI validation and Qubes calibration control traffic only.

failuresLessons: The previous implementation had workload-bound primitives and integration tests, but the executable CLI did not wire them together; component completeness did not imply production-path completeness.
Resource calibration evidence is only meaningful when workload generation is part of the same fail-closed execution path as sampling.
